title: The Sun's Influence on Earth
seo_title: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: The Sun's Influence on Earth Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The Sun is the main source of energy for the Earth's systems: it warms the land, water and air unevenly, drives winds, ocean currents and the water cycle, and is the energy source of food chains; Earth's energy balance and the greenhouse effect. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 1, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): the Sun's energy, uneven heating, winds and the water cycle, albedo, and the energy balance. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun drives Earth's weather and climate.
key_sub: Dark surfaces absorb more sunlight than light surfaces.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun gives off energy as light and heat. Places near the equator get more direct sunlight than places near the poles. Land heats up and cools down faster than water, which causes sea breezes and land breezes.

Uneven heating drives winds, ocean currents and the water cycle. Light surfaces such as clouds and ice reflect sunlight (high albedo); dark surfaces such as forests and the ocean absorb it. The greenhouse effect keeps the Earth warm enough for life.

Example

Daytime at the beach: which way does the breeze blow?

Land heats faster.

Answer: from the sea to the land

Example

Which surface absorbs more sunlight, asphalt or white sand?

Dark colour

Answer: asphalt

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the greenhouse effect is always harmful.
  • Thinking the Sun heats the air directly more than the ground.
  • Thinking seasons are caused by the Earth's distance from the Sun.

sets.title: Sources of energy for Earth processes

items.q: Where does most of Earth's internal heat come from?
c: the Sun shining through the crust
radioactive decay of uranium, thorium and potassium, and heat left from Earth's formation
items.e: It flows out at about 47 terawatts.

items.q: Why do clouds both warm and cool Earth?
c: they reflect sunlight (cooling) and absorb and re-emit infrared (warming)
items.e: Low clouds mostly cool; high thin clouds mostly warm.

items.e: Different causes act on very different time scales.

items.q: What are the two main sources of energy for Earth processes?
